chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih al-Jawaz, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih. He said: I heard Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) saying:
Whoever says "God knows" regarding something that God does not know, the Throne trembles out of exaltation of God, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.إعظاما: Exaltation, glorification - denotes the magnitude of God's greatness that causes the Throne to tremble
key_terms.العرش: The Throne (Arsh) - The greatest of God's creations, symbolizing His sovereignty and dominion
key_terms.يعلم الله: "God knows" - an oath formula; using it falsely is a grave sin

ai.seo_question: What happens when someone falsely says "God knows" according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against falsely attributing knowledge to God regarding something that is not true. This hadith, narrated in the Friday assembly of Rabi al-Akhir 368 AH, conveys the theological gravity of claiming God knows something that He does not actually know -- meaning ascribing falsehood to the Divine. The trembling of the Throne symbolizes the enormity of such a statement in terms of divine transcendence.
